edits.old: - `lfuo-learning-review-guide-2024-stakeholder-engagement.md`, US Forest Service (*Learning From Unintended Outcomes and Learning Review Implementation Guide*, 2024). The most extensive stakeholder-engagement source in the corpus for incident-review work. Operationalises Just Culture as the precondition for honest accounts (trust, fairness, dignity; administrative-firewall commitment in delegation of authority). Stakeholder map: FLA team roles (Process Coach, Team Leader, Lead Facilitator, Storyteller/Writer-Editor, Subject-Matter Experts/Peers, Technical Specialists, NTDP equipment SMEs, Human Performance experts, Union Representative, Documentation Specialist), participant categories (directly involved, supervisors, project leaders, Delegating Officials, families, cooperators, interagency partners, regulators, community of practice). Trust-bridge stakeholders (Family Liaison, Hospital Liaison, CISM Coordinator, CAP Coordinator, EAP, agency representative, IMT liaison, regional/state office, cooperator liaison). Facilitation discipline: Ten Principles and Agreements; "you are not your point of view" opening; "exploit points of departure" without adjudicating; "listen for the silent voice"; encourage sensemaking not adjudication; deflection-question protocol for emotional recall; two-interviewer team with intimidation caveat; daily team debrief. Restorative justice (Dekker & Breakey 2016) as an engagement modality after serious accidents. Two-phase readback for story validation. Community-of-practice focus groups for Learning Review recommendation vetting. Two distinct learning products (Organizational Learning Product for senior leadership, Field Learning Product for district/field). Concurrent investigations insulated but supported (Morning Briefing pattern). Public domain (17 USC §105) — no copyright propagation. Best paired with the NHS Just Culture Guide distillation (for the structured culpability decision tree), the OpenStax Organizational Behavior distillation (for group dynamics and conflict), and the OpenStax Business Ethics distillation (for normative frames on stakeholder claims).

edits.old: - `ssdl-systems-thinking-foundations-stakeholder-engagement.md`, Social System Design Lab / Brown School at Washington University in St. Louis (*Methods Briefs Series 1: Systems Thinking Foundations*, 2021; five briefs — 1.02 Complex Problems / 1.03 Mental Models / 1.05 Feedback Perspective / 1.06 Accumulations / 1.07 System Archetypes). Stakeholder dynamics as system structure rather than individual choice. Multi-stakeholder conflicting-goals as structural feature of complex problems (1.02); blindfolded-elephant parable as stakeholder-engagement frame (1.03); Group Model Building (citing Hovmand 2014) as the named participatory method; mental-models stickiness *especially among the unaffected* as a structural warning about whose model is shaping the conversation; trust as a stock not a flow (1.06) with the "blank slate" failure mode reframed for stakeholders arriving with accumulated history; feedback thinking applied to unexpected stakeholder responses (1.05); four of the five Brief 1.07 archetypes as stakeholder dynamics — *Success to the Successful* (resource-allocation inequity between groups), *Shifting the Burden* (symptomatic engagement that locks in failure), *Drifting Goals* (quiet aspiration-lowering), *Limits to Growth* (engagement scaling past capacity), plus *Fixes that Fail* applied to engagement strategy itself. Archetypes-can-reinforce-expert/novice warning as direct caution to the practitioner about their own positioning. Pairs with Barbrook-Johnson & Penn for methods-level systems-mapping engagement; Brief 1.07's acknowledgements name Senge (*The Fifth Discipline*, *Schools that Learn*) among recommended resources. **CC BY-SA 4.0 — copyleft propagation.**
